entities.name: Göbekli Tepe
entities.label: Place
entities.summary: A Neolithic archaeological site in southeastern Turkey, dated to c. 9500 BCE — making it the oldest known monumental architecture in the world. Its massive carved T-shaped pillars, built by hunter-gatherers before agriculture, overturned the assumption that complex architecture required settled civilization. Göbekli Tepe suggests ritual and religion may have driven the transition to farming, not the reverse.
